text:
maya: Heads-up — forecasting shows a ~2.3x GPU-hour spike week before Black Friday for hosted customers in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Numbers pulled from billing-proj and the demand model.
oscar: yikes. Is that forecasted for realtime inference or batch training? can we get breakdown by priority tiers?
maya: Mostly inference (~90%), and ~70% of that is many low-p99 requests from high-concurrency endpoints. Dedicated tenants are ~18% of the extra load, shared pool covers the rest.
srinivas: chart: https://grafana.company/dashboard/gpu-forecast (posted). fragmentation metric at cluster level is currently 23% for our 4xA100 fleet.
infra-bot: snapshot uploaded: /artifacts/gpuforecast-1765001234.png
leah: Immediate mitigations I suggest: 1) temporarily raise dedicated pool autoscale cap for top-tier tenants; 2) enable cross-region bursting for non latency-sensitive routes; 3) gate big batch training to off-peak windows; 4) enable soft-colocate scheduling for 48h trial.
oscar: Cross-region bursting adds egress and replication overhead. any rough egress numbers?
maya: rough calc: projected extra ~120k GPU-hours during surge. If we shift 10% traffic cross-region and each model pulls ~50GB/day, ballpark +$12k egress/week. finance needs to confirm.
srinivas: Fragmentation is the bigger immediate waste — 23% means many small slices. I want to try a proportional-fair bin-packing heuristic + soft-colocate to reduce headroom waste. Also consider relaxing strict tenant isolation for low-priority workloads.
leah: Can we do a short scheduler tweak: prefer same-tenant packing up to 0.85 fill, then spread to minimize eviction churn? that's low-risk and reversible.
oscar: Are there any upcoming rollouts that could create hotspots? eng-runtime has a KV-cache change that might double memory for some endpoints.
maya: yes, runtime canary scheduled tomorrow in us-west-2. propose throttling canary or moving it to a smaller region until load eases.
ops-oncall: also seeing occasional network tail latencies in us-west-2 peering -> could make cross-region SLOs worse if we burst. note to monitor net-tail metric.
srinivas: Proposed short playbook (quick):
- step 1: increase shared burst limit by +10% immediately (short window)
- step 2: enable soft-colocate policy for low-priority tenants for 24-48h
- step 3: enforce large batch jobs to night windows with 1.5x batching recommendations
- step 4: increase reserve pool for SLA tenants by 5% to avoid immediate evictions
I'll open a scheduler PR with config snippet: ```policy:
  soft_colocate: true
  colocate_threshold: 0.85
  eviction_grace: 30s
  tenant_priority_weights:
    sla: 1.0
    standard: 0.7
    free: 0.3```
maya: also request cost guard rails — add an alert if projected committed spend > 110% of monthly budget and notify finance + eng-ops.
leah: I'll notify finance and customer success for top customers; ops-oncall, can you run a traffic replay dry-run tonight to simulate the playbook?
ops-oncall: will run replay at 04:00 PT against the scheduler sandbox, will post results to #eng-infra and attach diffs.
oscar: If fragmentation reduction is insufficient, fallback option: spin a temporary spot/preemptible pool for background indexing and non-urgent workloads. lower cost but risk of preemption.
maya: timeline: implement soft-colocate + bump burst cap in the next 3 hours, run the replay overnight, review metrics and eviction rate tomorrow morning 08:30 PT. :thumbsup:
